title: A Codex test command that outlives the exec tool's initial yield and finishes through a polled exec session gets no host record: TermAl never observes its end
outcome: A recognised test command that Codex runs in the foreground is recorded with its real outcome (passed, failed, or a named refusal) whether it finishes inside the exec tool's initial yield or later through polling of the same exec session (write_stdin / host-process-wait). TermAl observes the command's end from whatever event or output the Codex app-server delivers for a polled completion, and attributes it to the original command's check. w-aec234e3f7d0's Unknown closure then remains only for a true missing end.
acceptance: The holder's note identifies, with file:line in TermAl and the Codex app-server event sequence observed, why a command completed through a polled exec session produces no end that TermAl attributes to its check, using the occurrences below.

A test drives a recognised Codex command whose end arrives through the polled-session path and shows no record on unchanged code, then the correct verification record after the fix; a test also shows that a command finishing within the initial yield is still recorded exactly once.
The full gate passes on the exact committed tree.

completion.summary: Landed triple commit 23e77889dd2f2f2eeb4ba650e9bfb7c342773e80 on origin/master, fast-forward from bd839153; exact-tree gate, review pair, and fresh acceptance evaluation are recorded.
